headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 24 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: The Iran-backed Houthi group launched an attack on King Khalid International Airport, affecting numerous Bangladeshi expatriates and pilgrims.
details: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and 24 others injured in an attack by the Iran-backed Houthi armed group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The identities of all casualties have been confirmed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates' Welfare.

The deceased were identified as Md Shahed Ahmed from Bogura and Md Nasrullah Badarpuri from Cumilla. Shahed was a plumber returning to his workplace in Jeddah, while Nasrullah was on an Umrah pilgrimage awaiting a transit flight to Jeddah.

Among the 24 injured Bangladeshis, 11 are Saudi-based workers and 13 were traveling on Umrah visas. They are currently receiving treatment in various hospitals across Riyadh, with the Bangladesh Embassy maintaining close contact with hospital authorities to ensure their care.

Three Bangladeshis, Hafez Hasan, Kazi Nurullah, and Md Omar Faruk, are in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), with their conditions reported as stable. Many of the injured were also transiting through Riyadh on their way to Jeddah for work or pilgrimage.

The attack also disrupted flight operations, leaving approximately 500 Bangladeshi passengers stranded at Riyadh airport. The embassy is actively collecting detailed information on all injured individuals and ensuring they receive proper medical attention.

headline_marked: [[Four remanded over defacing Rabindranath Tagore mural]] in Dhaka, accused of inciting hatred
headline: Four remanded over defacing Rabindranath Tagore mural in Dhaka, accused of inciting hatred
summary: A Dhaka court has remanded four individuals, including Rashtra Sanglap Forum President ANM Ayas, in connection with the defacement of a Rabindranath Tagore mural and alleged incitement of religious hatred.
details: A Dhaka court has placed Rashtra Sanglap Forum President ANM Ayas on a three-day remand in a case involving criminal conspiracy and inciting enmity between classes and religious hatred. The court order followed a police request for a 10-day remand.

Sakibul Hasan was also remanded for three days, while Sujon Mia and Marzia Khandaker Rimi received two-day remands each in the same case. Police had filed the case against Ayas and his three associates earlier that day at Shahbagh Police Station.

The four were detained on Saturday for their alleged involvement in attempting to deface a mural of Rabindranath Tagore. The incident occurred on a wall opposite the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Segunbagicha, Dhaka.

The mural was part of a Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) initiative to beautify a boundary wall after clearing hawkers from the footpath. It depicted Bangladesh's art, culture, and literature, featuring prominent figures.

According to the police report, Ayas had announced on October 9 his intention to whitewash the mural. The next day, he and the other accused went to the site where Rimi smeared black ink over the depiction of Nobel laureate poet Rabindranath Tagore.
Rimi is also accused of attempting to incite religious hatred in connection with the upcoming Durga Puja. This action, as per the report, aimed to create discord and undermine communal harmony.

The DSCC's project, which began on October 5, included portraits of 10 significant contributors to the country's art, literature, and culture. These figures include Rabindranath Tagore, Kazi Nazrul Islam, Zainul Abedin, and Satyajit Ray.
